name: STM8S103F3P6
description: 8-bit STM8-core microcontroller in a 20-pin TSSOP with 8 KB flash, 1 KB SRAM, 640 B data EEPROM and a 16 MHz max clock. It includes a 10-bit ADC, UART, SPI, I2C, timers with PWM and true data EEPROM, all in a sub-dollar part programmed over a single-wire SWIM interface. Hobbyists meet it on the famous ~$0.30 'STM8S103 minimum system' breakout boards as a cheaper alternative to AVR/STM32. Standout traits: bargain price, on-chip EEPROM, and 5 V operation.

pins.name: VCAP
pins.description: 1.8 V internal regulator decoupling; connect external cap to VSS, do not supply externally

pins.name: PC3
pins.description: GPIO PC3; TIM1_CH3, TLI top-level interrupt

pins.name: PC4
pins.description: GPIO PC4; TIM1_CH4, CLK_CCO, AIN2 ADC

pins.name: PD1
pins.description: GPIO PD1; SWIM single-wire debug/programming pin

pins.name: PD3
pins.description: GPIO PD3; AIN4 ADC, TIM2_CH2, ADC_ETR

extra.timers: advanced TIM1, TIM2, TIM4; PWM capable

typical_application: Ultra-low-cost control tasks such as battery monitors, simple PWM/motor control, and EEPROM-logging gadgets on the cheap STM8S103 breakout board.
gotchas: programmed via single-wire SWIM, NOT SWD/JTAG; you need an ST-Link with the SWIM pin (PD1), not a generic SWD-only debugger
VCAP (pin 8) is the internal 1.8 V regulator output and needs a ~1 uF cap to VSS; never feed it external power or leave it floating
toolchain is not Arduino-native; use SDCC + stm8flash or ST's STVD/Cosmic, a steeper setup than AVR/STM32
default clock is the 16 MHz HSI divided by 8, so the part boots at 2 MHz until the clock prescaler is changed
PB4/PB5 (I2C pins) are true open-drain only and cannot source high, requiring external pull-ups
tiny RAM (1 KB) and flash (8 KB) limit firmware size; large libraries will not fit
